activities.anchor: the document by which the pope supposedly received his temporal power
activities.caption: find the faulty line — Valla's philology
activities.name: rrVallaSpot

config.prompt: One line of this humanism summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Petrarch hunted manuscripts across Europe; the programme was to recover, edit and read properly the texts of antiquity.
Lorenzo Valla proved in 1440 that the Donation of Constantine was genuine.
His critical philology is the ancestor of modern source criticism.
It quietly taught Europe that authorities could be checked against evidence.
Luther would later take exactly those philological tools and demand a reform the hierarchy could not contain.
config.correction: Valla proved the Donation a forgery — by noticing that its Latin could not have been written in the fourth century.
config.why: That is the humanists' quiet revolution: not against religion (nearly all were devout Christians), but for checking authority against evidence — and Luther later aimed the same tools at the hierarchy itself.

activities.caption: line up the mathematics of seeing, earliest first
activities.name: rrPerspectiveOrder

config.prompt: Linear perspective's milestones — order them, earliest first:
items: Brunelleschi's panel demonstration in the Florence cathedral square — c. 1420
Masaccio painting with the new depth, within a generation
the dome of Florence cathedral completed without centring scaffolds — 1436
config.why: A geometric method for projecting three-dimensional space onto a flat panel — parallel lines converging on vanishing points — made painting partly an engineering discipline, and the artist rose from craftsman to celebrity genius.

config.prompt: By 1500, roughly how many books had Europe's print shops produced?
config.why: An estimated 20 million, from roughly 1,000 European print shops — more than all the scribes of the previous thousand years, at collapsing prices.
config.context: A book fell from roughly the price of a small farm to that of a few days' wages over the following century.

activities.caption: bet before you read on — did the press cause it?
activities.name: rrPressPredict

config.q: Did the printing press cause the Reformation?
choices: Yes — without print there could have been no split
No — the press was the condition (rapid, identical transmission); the causes were the theological grievance and the political protection of German princes
Yes — printing spread true ideas faster than error
config.why: Without the grievance, the press prints nothing worth banning; without the press, the grievance stays local, as Hus's and Wycliffe's had. It is the combination, not either half alone, that broke Christendom.

activities.anchor: then radicalised into a full alternative theology
activities.caption: line up the Reformation's chain, earliest first
activities.name: rrReformOrder

config.prompt: From debate notice to European event — order these, earliest first:
items: Luther circulates the Ninety-five Theses against indulgences — 31 October 1517
summoned to Augsburg, condemned by Pope Leo X — 1518
excommunicated, and refuses to recant before the Emperor at the Diet of Worms — 1521
the Peace of Augsburg writes the split into law: each ruler chooses his lands' faith — 1555
the Thirty Years' War devastates the Holy Roman Empire — 1618–1648
config.why: What began as a routine academic debate notice became a European event because, for the first time, a churchman's argument could outrun the church's messengers — Frederick the Wise's protection kept the author alive to write more.
